editorial.marketOverview: Friday's Nasdaq and semiconductor selling remains pronounced, but a later Reuters snapshot showed Nasdaq -0.93%, SOX -3.7% and Nvidia -2.2%, less severe than the earlier Reuters account of Nasdaq-100 near -2% and SOX -5.1%. These are asynchronous intraday reports, not verified same-time cross-asset observations or closing prices. The narrower declines are consistent with partial stabilization, not proof of a durable reversal.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 13:39 EST repository snapshot, the later Reuters account suggests some moderation of the semiconductor rout. AP separately reported Brent settling at $95.84 and a 10-year yield near 5.15%, while Reuters' earlier oil report had Brent $95.77 and WTI $88.57. The Open Watch feed remains at 163 curated events as of 18:24:41 UTC. None of these inputs establishes a distinct new three-day regime change.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The market continues to discount uncertainty around Nvidia leadership, AI-infrastructure financing and higher discount rates. Softer monthly PPI (+0.3% versus +0.4% expected) did not prevent selling, while 6.5% annual producer inflation and reported Fed-hike expectations limit relief. SOX still materially lags the broad market in the later Reuters report. An 11% reported probability of a 50bp December hike is secondary reporting, not a fresh live FedWatch reading.
editorial.threeDayPath: For Friday November 13, confirmation at the cash close matters more than fluctuating intraday reports. Monday November 16 is the key test of whether Friday's semiconductor decline extends or produces an oversold bounce. Tuesday November 17 remains exposed to AI-related corporate catalysts and Fed repricing. Bearish elevated downside remains the base case, though a tactical rebound is plausible and should not be mistaken for sustained leadership without breadth and volatility confirmation.
editorial.bullCase: A close materially off Friday's lows followed by synchronized QQQ and SOX outperformance, positive breadth, lower volatility and easing Treasury yields would weaken the bearish scenario. Limited PPI relief and resilient nontech groups can support a bounce, but the available evidence is not sufficient to upgrade the bias.
editorial.bearCase: A weak Friday close and a Monday break below Friday lows would validate continuation. Persistent SOX weakness, pressure on AI-financing-linked equities, negative breadth and high yields could magnify Nasdaq downside despite softer monthly PPI. No exact probability is assigned because key synchronized measures are missing.
editorial.watchNext: Obtain verified Friday closing levels and timestamp-aligned QQQ, SOX, VXN/VIX, Nasdaq breadth, 10Y and 2Y yields, Brent and WTI, and live CME FedWatch. Recheck the curated Open Watch feed and confirm actual issuer calendars for next week's AI events before attributing market moves to those catalysts.
